corpus.embeddingType: synthetic clustered unit vectors, NOT real corpus content

primaryError: vector index: unable to update global metadata table

rootCauseAssessment.reasoning: Original benchmark script wrapped ALL client.execute/batch calls (including CREATE INDEX) in a uniform network-error retry. Attempt 1 of CREATE INDEX for default/uncompressed DiskANN on the full 20,652x768 table got an ambiguous 'fetch failed' (client-side, does not prove the server never received/started the request); the wrapper retried 550ms later; attempt 2 failed with 'unable to update global metadata table' - consistent with the retry colliding with a still-in-flight or partially-committed first attempt (H3+H4).

postFailureState.decision: STOP retrying cleanup. Preserve as forensic evidence. Move all further benchmark configs to differently-named tables (never touch bench_default_uncompressed again) in the SAME database (justified fallback tier - no platform API access to create new Turso databases, only a database-scoped connection token).

researchFindings.exactErrorTextInGithubIssues: NOT FOUND in tursodatabase/libsql or tursodatabase/turso via GitHub search API across multiple query angles
researchFindings.relatedHistory: Confirmed real historical shadow-table consistency bugs exist (closed PR #1641: 'fix behaviour of VACUUM for vector indices to make rowid consistent between shadow tables and base table'), supporting plausibility of the mechanism without confirming this exact incident
researchFindings.interpretation: Absence of a matching report supports the self-inflicted-retry-collision hypothesis over a widely-known platform bug

storageModel.note: extrapolated from N=300 measurement prior to full scaling-ladder results

postFixFindings.codeFix: CREATE INDEX now goes through executeOnce() with zero automatic retry. default_uncompressed permanently excluded from the active config set. Scaling ladder (1000/5000/10000/20652) added. Structured per-run report block added. Error classification added.

n5000_diskann_f8_and_f16_default_timeout.criticalDifferenceFromOriginalIncident: ZERO orphaned structures left behind (confirmed via direct sqlite_master inspection immediately after) - a clean timeout, not corrupted partial state. Because CREATE INDEX was never retried, there was no second attempt to collide with the first.

n5000_extended_timeout_retest.method: Single un-retried CREATE INDEX attempt, client fetch timeout extended to 20min (later 30min) via undici setGlobalDispatcher (NOT a custom fetch injection - that approach hit a Request/Response cross-realm bug, same class as the one fixed in tests/integration/knowledgeStore-turso-cloud.test.ts)
n5000_extended_timeout_retest.result: BOTH bench_diskann_f8_5000_idx and bench_diskann_f16_5000_idx completed successfully server-side, confirmed by direct sqlite_master + row-count + functional-query inspection after a session restart lost local log tracking (Turso DB state is external/persistent, unaffected)
n5000_extended_timeout_retest.f8SpotCheckRecall: 10/10 on a single query, consistent with the table's data matching the run's own freshly-rebuilt bench_exact
n5000_extended_timeout_retest.f16SpotCheckRecall: 0/10 across 5 queries - DIAGNOSED AS STALE CROSS-RUN DATA, not a real quality problem: bench_diskann_f16_5000 was built by an earlier (pre-restart) full-ladder run's corpus, while bench_exact was later rebuilt fresh (different random corpus, no fixed seed) by a subsequent partial single-config run that only touched diskann_f8. Both stale tables (f8_5000 and f16_5000) were dropped cleanly and quickly (1.9s, 13.0s - notably NOT hung like the original incident's corrupted table, confirming these were healthy structures, just semantically stale) and are being rebuilt together in one consistent run.
n5000_extended_timeout_retest.conclusion: N=5000 build TIME succeeds given enough client-side patience (exact duration not captured due to session restart, bounded to <20min for f8/f16). This is a genuine, reportable finding regardless of the recall artifact: default client/library timeouts (~5min) are insufficient for index builds at this scale, with real implications for any production architecture that would build/rebuild this index synchronously (e.g. inside a single Convex action).
